title: Work IQ: Microsoft IQ as a unified intelligence layer for agents
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and clearly separates the planned release from existing Work IQ capabilities. The documented admin paths and spending-policy API are supported, and the page acknowledges the differing write defaults and service-principal setup guidance.

The roadmap description consists of the single sentence quoted in the briefing.

claims.claim: The Microsoft IQ documentation hub describes Microsoft IQ as a unified intelligence layer for enterprise AI.
claims.quote: Microsoft IQ is a unified intelligence layer for enterprise AI

claims.claim: The hub lists four capabilities: Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ and Web IQ.
claims.quote: Microsoft IQ brings together four interconnected capabilities:

claims.claim: The hub describes Work IQ as understanding how employees work, including people, collaboration and workflows.
claims.quote: Work IQ provides live understanding of how employees work, with context on people, collaboration, and workflows.

claims.claim: Fabric IQ provides the live state of the business.
claims.quote: Fabric IQ provides the live state of the business, so agents understand business entities and their relationships, properties, actions, and rules.

claims.claim: Foundry IQ provides curated institutional knowledge.
claims.quote: Foundry IQ provides curated institutional knowledge on the context of policies, authoritative documents, and reusable knowledge bases.

claims.claim: Web IQ provides fresh intelligence from the web.
claims.quote: Web IQ provides AI systems and agents with fresh, real-world intelligence from across the web.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly identified whether this roadmap release is the Microsoft IQ hub or a particular change to Work IQ.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ Microsoft IQ roadmap 570870 licensing default tenant policy API; "Microsoft IQ" "570870" default licensing preview January 2027 November 2026. Opened Microsoft IQ hub and Work IQ overview; read roadmap record.

claims.claim: Work IQ lets agents access and reason over organisational and business data, context and tools with permission-aware governance.
claims.quote: Work IQ is a workplace intelligence layer that enables agents to access and reason over organizational and business data, context, and tools. It continuously builds a semantic understanding across Microsoft 365 and external systems with built-in, permission-aware governance.

claims.claim: Work IQ exposes A2A, remote MCP and REST API endpoints.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Every Work IQ request runs in a specific user's context.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The user's existing permissions limit what Work IQ can return or do.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.

claims.claim: Work IQ includes productivity data from Microsoft 365 applications.
claims.quote: In addition to productivity data from Microsoft 365 applications, Work IQ also includes business and workflow data from Dynamics 365 and Power Platform.

claims.claim: Work IQ includes business and workflow data from Dynamics 365 and Power Platform.
claims.quote: In addition to productivity data from Microsoft 365 applications, Work IQ also includes business and workflow data from Dynamics 365 and Power Platform.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy complements rather than replaces Entra authentication, OAuth permissions and the user's Microsoft 365 permissions.
claims.quote: For Work IQ MCP, policy governance doesn't replace Microsoft Entra authentication, OAuth permissions, or the signed-in user's existing Microsoft 365 permissions.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy cannot grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing access.
claims.quote: Policy can't grant access beyond what the signed-in user is already allowed to access.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP tools support reading, creating, updating and deleting data.
claims.quote: It provides tools that enable agents to read, create, update, and delete Microsoft 365 entities

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP tenant-policy documentation says mutation operations are disallowed by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio Microsoft Copilot harness guide separately says write operations are on by default.
claims.quote: Write operations are on by default. Your organization's permissions and policies still apply.

claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported Work IQ MCP mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply across the tenant.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users get Work IQ in Copilot experiences and agents, with usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents. It is subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.

claims.claim: Users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence are billed for Work IQ based on usage.
claims.quote: Users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license are billed based on usage.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: The Work IQ enablement guide lists a usage-based billing plan set up in Copilot Studio as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: A usage-based billing plan set up in Copilot Studio with an Azure subscription and resource group assigned.

claims.claim: The enablement guide requires an Azure subscription and resource group assigned to that billing plan.
claims.quote: A usage-based billing plan set up in Copilot Studio with an Azure subscription and resource group assigned.

claims.claim: The enablement guide names the Global Administrator role for one-time Work IQ setup.
claims.quote: A user with Global Administrator role for the one-time Work IQ setup

claims.claim: The one-time setup described in the enablement guide creates the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote: This section creates the Work IQ service principal in your organization, which provisions the Work IQ resource so your applications can request tokens for it.

claims.claim: The MCP overview also says the Work IQ service principal is automatically created on first use.
claims.quote: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically in the tenant when you use Work IQ for the first time.

claims.claim: Manual service-principal provisioning can be needed to configure Work IQ MCP policy before any MCP use.
claims.quote: In some corner cases, such as configuring Work IQ MCP policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center before any MCP use in the tenant, the service principal might not exist yet and policy configuration can fail.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy settings are at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Spending and consumption for Work IQ API are managed under Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost management.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft admin center, Copilot > Cost management, admins can monitor Copilot Credit consumption and manage spending associated with the supported services such as Cowork, running apps hosted on the Copilot Managed Runtime, and Work IQ API.

claims.claim: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies lists spending policies.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. ... List spendingPolicies | GET `/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies` | Get a list of spending policies.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP Policy tab is conditional on availability.
claims.quote: On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: Initial Work IQ MCP policy control is tenant-level.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control.

claims.claim: Per-user, per-app, per-agent and scenario-specific policy templates are not part of the initial MCP policy control surface.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.claim: Microsoft says more granular MCP policy controls might be added later.
claims.quote: More granular controls and policy templates might be added later based on customer requests, feedback, and usage.

claims.claim: The tenant's Cost management dashboard supports spending policies, spending limits and alerts for supported services.
claims.quote: Configure identity and resource-based spending policies. ... Set spending limits for supported users, environments, and agents. ... Configure policy alerts and user-level threshold notifications.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout

claims.quote: Review consumption by spending policy, user, group, agent, service, and funding source.

claims.quote: Spending policies can automatically apply to future supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents.

claims.claim: The Cost Management API is beta, subject to change and unsupported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.
claims.quote: Creating a spending policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role at runtime.
